references.text: The almond tree (שָׁקֵד) is mentioned as a symbol of vigilance and God's swift fulfillment of His promises, similar to Aaron's staff that blossomed with almonds.
The lampstand in the tabernacle was decorated with almond flowers, linking together the theme of almonds and priestly service.
The description of the lampstand's almond-shaped bowls, buds, and flowers shows the connection between almonds and holy service.
The following verse, where Aaron's staff is to be kept as a sign against the rebels, confirms the affirmation of Aaron's priesthood.
Jeremiah sees an almond branch (מַקֵּל שָׁקֵד) as a sign that God watches over His word to fulfill it.
A shoot shall spring up from the stump of Jesse, thematically resembling the miraculous sprouting of Aaron's staff.
The book of Hebrews mentions Aaron's staff that blossomed, kept in the ark of the covenant as a testimony to God's choice.
